text:
maya: Heads-up — production shard node 7 hit OOMs twice this morning during long chat sessions. Pattern looks familiar (slow steady growth then abrupt spike).
tess: Can you drop the quick profiler output? wondering if this is fragmentation or retained refs.
maya: Profiling snippet: retained by KV tombstones ~28%, active entries ~45%, unknown roots ~12%. Flamegraph points to scorer::lease_holder path.
rahul: If lease_holder keeps a strong ref while scoring streaming responses that's a leak vector. We had a similar regression last quarter.
jun: I ran a quick heap-scan on staging and reproduced tombstone buildup after ~20k inserts. Attaching command for others: ```./tools/heapscan --node shard7 --threshold 90s --out /tmp/scan-2111.json```
leo: Two proposed mitigations: 1) Add a short default TTL for ephemeral cache entries; 2) introduce a weak_ptr path for scorer leases so GC can collect. Both have tradeoffs for tail latency.
tess: Let's make a concrete action list with owners and deadlines:
  - rahul -> implement weak_ptr lease + opt-in TTL (default 10m) on scorer path. target: 2026-04-02
  - jun -> create a scheduled heap-scan job that triggers when growth > 50MB over 2m, notify eng-runtime. target: 2026-04-01
  - leo -> experiment with allocator: reduce slab size to 16KB and run fragmentation benchmark, post CSV. target: 2026-04-03
  - infra/sre -> add an eviction hysteresis alarm (warn at 70%, critical at 88%). owner: sre-bot. target: 2026-04-01
  - maya -> run a canary rollout plan for TTL+weak path to 5% traffic, monitor p99 and memory. target: 2026-04-06
rahul: My dev plan: add feature flag `scorer.use_lease_weakref` + `scorer.default_ttl_seconds=600`. Local unit tests + staging 24h soak. PR draft soon.
jun: Reproducer CI job suggestion: a long-chat-simulator that holds streams open for 15min while doing random inserts/evicts. If we can make that part of pre-merge for the scorer package it would catch regressions.
leo: For allocator experiments I'll compare internal compaction time, free-list fragmentation, and p99 latency. Expect some p99 tradeoffs.
sre-bot: alert rule created: KV_tombstone_pressure (warn 70%, crit 88%) -> notify eng-runtime-oncall.
tess: Note: avoid aggressive TTLs that cause cache churn for hot entries. We'll need metrics for cache hit rate before changing defaults.
maya: I ran a quick estimate — TTL=10m should reduce retained tombstones by ~18% in current workload based on sampling. rahul please include numbers in PR.
rahul: Draft PR link (WIP): https://git.internal/rw/serving/pulls/3348 — includes flags, unit tests, and a small benchmark.
jun: I'll add the heap-scan job YAML to infra-tests repo and wire up a webhook to the runbook. Command snippet: ```
- name: tombstone-heap-scan
  schedule: "cron(*/5 * * * *)"
  trigger_if: ">=50MB_growth_2m"
  action: /tools/heapscan --out artifacts/heap-{{ts}}.json
```
leo: If we see p99 regressions in canary, we can fallback via rollout policy (auto-disable flag). Keep rollback plan in PR description.
tess: Scheduling a 30m follow-up tomorrow 9am PST to review first PR and heap-scan results. Invite sent.
maya: I'll update the incident postmortem with these action items and owners. Please add links to PRs and CSVs as they appear.
rahul: Will mark PR ready after staging soak and add benchmark graphs.
leo: I'll post allocator experiment results by EOD next Friday.
jun: Will push the CI reproducer this week.
sre-bot: oncall notified: eng-runtime; current incident ticket #INC-2026-2111 created.
tess: Great. Keeping this thread as the central tracker. Ping if blockers appear. :white_check_mark:
